text.tspan: Predicting Interstitial Electron Localization and Void Connectivity for Electride Screening
A void-centered machine-learning and geometric framework for characterizing electrides
A crystal where electrons act as anions.
Extra electrons sit in the voids between atoms.
The electron localization function runs from 0 to 1. A high value in a void means a trapped electron.
Each crystal needs its own DFT calculation.
screen crystals for electrides from structure alone, without DFT on every candidate. We built two void-centered tools and tested each one separately.
A graph neural network predicts ELF at individual voids from the surrounding atoms

text.tspan: a void alone predicts almost nothing (RMSE 0.140).
trained on ELFNet (compressed hydrides), so not yet tested on known electrides. Rare voids with ELF ≥ 0.7 are under-predicted.
Geometry alone recovers the dimensionality of known electrides above chance

g.text: must fit to pass through a neck
It runs on through every cell

text.tspan: Schematic of an illustrative crystal, not a real material
Open space is not the same as electrons
Same open channel, different electrons: only ELF at the necks tells 1D from 0D.
Predicting ELF at voids and mapping void connectivity build a screen that can separate structural from electronic dimensionality.
A foundation, not yet a validated electride classifier.
A prediction target at specific crystal voids
An atom–void graph that keeps chemical and geometric context
An exact connectivity screen for void networks
A path to combining geometry with electronic evidence
Run DFT on known electrides to test the GNN
